summary: Peter Lindegger-Stauffer (1933–2004) worked in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He received an honorary Ph.D. from the University of Fribourg in ~1998 and served as curator at the Tibet Institute Rikon from 1967 to 1974.

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Pennsylvania (1983–1990) under George Cardona. He founded and directs the Sanskrit Library and held posts at Brown University and IIIT Hyderabad.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and doctoral supervisor Ninian Smart, and he taught Nicolas Revire.
Peter Moran is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who studied at Tufts University and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Washington under supervisor Charles Keyes.

Peter N. Gregory is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard University in 1981 under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Kuroda Institute, and Smith College.

Peter Nicolas Harting (1892–1970) was a linguist and Indologist who earned an M.A. and Ph.D. at Utrecht University under Willem Caland. He held posts in Dutch at London, Bedford College, and Oxford, before serving as Professor of English at Groningen and Amsterdam.

Peter Percival (1803–1882) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Principal of Jaffna Central College (1832–1851), taught at St Augustine's College, and became Registrar at the University of Madras and Professor at Presidency University in 1856.

Peter Peterson (1847–1899) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Oxford under Theodor Aufrecht, Monier Monier-Williams, and Max Müller. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and Registrar at the University of Mumbai.

Peter Schreiner is an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Paul Hacker at the University of Münster (1968–1972) and habilitated at Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, SOAS University of London, and the University of Zurich.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his M.A. at the University of Washington in 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Dieter Schuh. He worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and later held the chair for Tibetology at Bonn.

Peter Scott Noble (1899–1987) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Aberdeen and Cambridge under Edward James Rapson and Peter Giles. He was Professor of Latin at Leeds, Regius Professor at Aberdeen, and Principal of King's College London.

Peter Skilling is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed his Ph.D. at EPHE. He founded the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation and has held posts at EFEO, Chulalongkorn University, and Lumbini International Research Institute.

Peter Stewart is an art historian and Indologist who studied at Clare College, Cambridge. He has held appointments at the Courtauld Institute of Art and the Classical Art Research Centre, and became Associate Professor at the University of Oxford in 2011.
Peter Stumpf (1940–1977) was a linguist and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt (1959–1968) under Werner Thomas, where he subsequently served as an assistant until 1977.
Peter Thomi is an Indologist who studied under Alfred Bloch and served as director of the Institut für Indologie Wichtrach (attested 1995).

Peter Zieme is a scholar of Central Asian languages and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University. He worked at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR, Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences, and Free University of Berlin.

Peter van der Veer is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Groningen and Utrecht. He held professorships at Amsterdam, Utrecht, and Pennsylvania, and served as Director at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Peter von Bohlen (1796–1840) was an Indologist who studied under Gesenius, Schlegel, Freytag, and Bopp at Halle, Bonn, and Berlin. He spent his academic career at the University of Königsberg, becoming an ordinary professor in 1828/1830.

Peter von Bradke (1853–1897) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Leo Meyer at Tartu, Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen, and Berthold Delbrück at Jena. He habilitated at the University of Giessen, where he became an extraordinary professor.
